title: Elton John Plays Rare Song 'Skyline Pigeon' in Brazil!
summary:
Have you ever heard a song that gives you goosebumps? Imagine being at a huge music festival and hearing a superstar play a song he hasn't performed in years—just for you!

That's what happened at Rock in Rio in Brazil on September 8, 2026. Elton John, the famous singer and piano player, performed a rare song called "Skyline Pigeon." He wrote it way back in 1969 with his songwriting partner Bernie Taupin. It was on his first album, Empty Sky.

Elton told the crowd, "This next song is the first good song I wrote with Bernie. And Brazil is the only place it's ever been popular, so here we go."

Why is it popular in Brazil? Well, in 1972, Elton re-recorded the song and it was used in a Brazilian soap opera called Carinhoso. That made it a big hit there! So Elton has played it mostly in Brazil, Ecuador, and Chile.

The song has beautiful lyrics about a bird wanting to fly free: "Turn me loose from your hands, let me fly to distant lands." Elton said the words sound like a hymn you'd sing in church, so he wrote music that sounds like one too.

Elton John stopped touring in 2023 after his big Farewell Yellow Brick Road tour. But he still plays special shows sometimes. This concert was a big deal because he hasn't played "Skyline Pigeon" live since 2019.

He's also working on a new album! So keep your ears open for more music from this legend. And if you ever get to hear "Skyline Pigeon" live, consider yourself lucky—it's a rare treat!
why_it_matters: Music can connect generations and countries, so learning the history behind an old song can make you feel closer to people who loved it before you were born.
